scope: V120 event_outbox/event_inbox owner-lease migration on an isolated MySQL 8.4.11 sandbox

environment.isolation: single-node Docker container, dedicated sandbox databases, no production connection

negative_execution.fixture: pre-create event_inbox index idx_event_inbox_status_lease on (status, id)
negative_execution.expected: V120 fails closed instead of accepting an incompatible lease index
negative_execution.actual_error: ERROR 1644 (45000) at line 250: V120 blocked: incompatible event_inbox lease index

defect_found_and_fixed.summary: The first sandbox rerun exposed that ordinary non-unique indexes were checked with MAX(non_unique) = 0, which is the unique-index value. The migration and verification checks were corrected to MAX(non_unique) = 1.
defect_found_and_fixed.initial_rerun_error: ERROR 1644 (45000) at line 250: V120 blocked: incompatible event_inbox lease index
defect_found_and_fixed.resolution: Only the ordinary-index predicate was corrected; column order, BTREE, non-prefix, and fail-closed checks remain strict.

conclusion.owner_fencing_application_evidence: H2/unit-level only; not proven by this migration sandbox run
limits: No production execution, production data, production topology, replication, failover, or load test was performed.
The negative case proves fail-closed behavior for one incompatible-index fixture, not every possible incompatible schema shape.
V120 migration success does not prove application-level owner fencing, lease timing, compensation, or reconciliation semantics.
